lead.label: 5e
lead.why: Abstract: 'compound 5e as the most potent bone anabolic agent, found to be active at 1 pM ... assessed for its osteogenic potential in vivo'.

reactions.conditions: Claisen-Schmidt: ketone (10 mmol) and aldehyde (10 mmol) in EtOH, NaOH (4 M), rt overnight; neutralised with 1 N HCl, precipitate filtered; 80%.
reactions.source: Experimental, General Synthesis of chalcones (2a-n) and entry 2e; Scheme 1 step (i)

reactions.conditions: Intramolecular oxa-Michael cyclisation: chalcone (0.01 mol) in EtOH, conc. H2SO4 added slowly, reflux 4-6 h; neutralised with sat. NaHCO3, EtOAc extraction; 74%.
reactions.source: Experimental, General Synthesis of 5'-nitro flavanones (3a-n) and entry 3e; Scheme 1 step (ii)

reactions.conditions: Fe powder (0.03 mol), CaCl2 (0.01 mol), EtOH/H2O, reflux 4-5 h; filtered over celite, EtOAc extraction; 89% (reddish oil).
reactions.source: Experimental, General Synthesis of 5'-amino flavanones (4a-n) and entry 4e; Scheme 1 step (iii)

reactions.conditions: Amine (0.01 mol) in CH2Cl2 at 0 C, Et3N added, then acid chloride (0.01 mol) in CH2Cl2, rt 2 h; workup, column (EtOAc/hexane); 84%.
reactions.source: Experimental, General Synthesis of galloyl conjugates (5a-n) and entry 5e; Scheme 1 step (iv)

notes: 4 steps (limit). No SI text was provided; the article's Experimental section was sufficient. 5e is racemic (stereocentre at C-2 not specified; later resolved by HPLC) so no stereo in SMILES. The printed names of the flavanone intermediates 3e and 4e say '4H-chromen-4-one' (which is the flavone oxidation level and would not match my SMILES under OPSIN) but their NMR (H-2 dd 5.86/5.46, H-3 dd) and the later 'chroman-4-one' names show they are 2,3-dihydro flavanones; my SMILES are the flavanones. The 4e NMR lists '2.78 (s, 3H)' where OMe (3.78) is meant. The aldehyde is not named in the general procedure ('the respective aldehyde'); 3-methoxybenzaldehyde is inferred from chalcone 2e's name. 3,4,5-Trimethoxybenzoyl chloride is not stated as purchased but is used without preparation. 'Reagents obtained from commercial sources'.
